newsitem.title: GERMANY: German politicians welcome Prague approval.
newsitem.headline: German politicians welcome Prague approval.

text.p: German politicians on Friday welcomed Friday's vote by Czech lower house of parliament to approve a post-World War Two reconciliation agreement between the two countries.
"After a long and difficult debate, the Czech parliament has taken a responsible and wise decision," Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in a statement.
"I welcome above all the fact that the decision, which was made by 131 votes to 59, reflects a solid consensus among democratic forces," Kinkel added.
The president of the German lower house, Rita Suessmuth, also welcomed the decision, saying "bilateral relations have now been placed on a solid political base".

Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the leader of Bavaria's Christian Social Union -- which has championed the cause of the so-called Sudeten Germans expelled from then-Czechoslovakia after the war -- was more reserved in his reaction.
Waigel told Reuters at a CSU meeting in Munich that Germany's treatment of the Czechs during the war had been wrong but that the Czechs also had to acknowledge their misdeeds.
